changes.old: Simulating the random events requires a rule for generating repeatable sample sequences. A [[**random seed**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} fixes the starting state of a pseudorandom generator so that a specified implementation can repeat its sample sequence.]{.definition-explanation} The seed controls which sequence is drawn; it does not set the intended firing-rate distribution. The code uses a trajectory index to choose that starting state.
changes.new: Simulated spike times are drawn by a program that generates a repeatable sequence of random-looking numbers. A [[**random seed**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} sets its starting state, allowing the same implementation and sequence of calls to reproduce those samples.]{.definition-explanation} The spike-generation rule specifies the intended distribution; the seed chooses the sample sequence.
changes.reason: Stage2: explain the generator role in ordinary words and keep the rate-model versus sample-sequence distinction.
